cars.description: 2018 Lamborghini Huracán Coupé in Sky Blue A Low-Mileage Naturally Aspirated V10 Supercar This 2018 Lamborghini Huracan for sale in Dubai is finished in an eye-catching Sky Blue exterior and paired with a timeless Black interior. Showing only 16,000 kilometres, it presents the original Huracán Coupé’s clean design and naturally aspirated V10 performance in a highly distinctive colour combination. Produced before the later Huracán EVO redesign, the 2018 model retains the pure exterior styling and more analogue cockpit associated with the first-generation car. Its combination of dramatic Lamborghini design, a responsive 5.2-litre V10 and everyday usability helped establish the Huracán as one of the defining modern supercars. Distinctive Sky Blue Exterior The Sky Blue finish brings a fresh character to the Huracán’s low and sharply sculpted bodywork. The bright colour highlights the angular front bumper, rising side profile and pronounced rear shoulders while contrasting effectively against the darker windows, air intakes and exterior details. At the front, narrow LED headlights sit above large cooling openings, giving the car an unmistakably focused appearance. The side profile is shaped by a sweeping line that flows from the front wheel arch towards the engine intakes, while the compact rear section places the visual emphasis on the mid-mounted V10. Unlike later and more aerodynamically aggressive Huracán variants, the original Coupé uses comparatively restrained surfaces. This gives its design a clarity that has aged particularly well. Timeless Black Interior The Black interior provides a composed contrast to the Sky Blue exterior. Its dark finish allows the cockpit’s angular architecture, metal controls and digital displays to take visual priority without competing with the exterior colour. Lamborghini designed the cabin around its “feel like a pilot” philosophy. The low seating position places the driver close to the centre of the car, while the primary controls are arranged around the steering wheel and centre console. An aviation-inspired cover protects the engine start button, and large paddles allow the driver to control the seven-speed transmission manually. The digital instrument display can change its presentation according to the selected driving mode, placing road, navigation or performance information directly ahead of the driver. 5.2-Litre Naturally Aspirated V10 Positioned behind the occupants is Lamborghini’s 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10. In the LP 610-4 Coupé configuration, the engine produces 610 CV at 8,250 rpm and sends power through the seven-speed Lamborghini Doppia Frizione dual-clutch transmission. The engine combines direct and multi-point fuel injection, providing precise fuel delivery while retaining the response and high-revving character for which Lamborghini’s V10 became known. Without turbochargers interrupting the relationship between the accelerator and engine, power builds progressively as the revs rise. Lamborghini quotes acceleration from 0–100 km/h in 3.2 seconds, 0–200 km/h in 9.9 seconds and a maximum speed exceeding 325 km/h for the LP 610-4 Coupé. These are manufacturer figures for the model and have not been independently measured for this particular vehicle. Complete specifications are available through Lamborghini’s official Huracán Coupé technical page . Seven-Speed Dual-Clutch Transmission The Lamborghini Doppia Frizione transmission uses two clutches to prepare the next gear before it is selected. This allows fast changes under acceleration while providing smoother operation during everyday driving. The driver can leave the transmission to operate automatically or select gears manually using the fixed steering-column paddles. This arrangement makes the Huracán manageable in urban conditions while retaining the direct involvement expected from a naturally aspirated supercar. All-Wheel-Drive Traction The Huracán LP 610-4 uses an electronically controlled all-wheel-drive system to manage its V10 performance. Torque can be distributed between the front and rear axles according to available grip, vehicle movement and the selected driving mode. This provides strong traction during acceleration while helping the car remain composed through faster corners. The system retains a rear-led character, ensuring that the Huracán still feels responsive rather than neutral or detached. Strada, Sport and Corsa Modes The ANIMA selector allows the driver to choose between Strada, Sport and Corsa. Each mode changes the response of the engine, transmission, stability control and other dynamic systems. Strada provides the most refined calibration for everyday use. Sport gives the car a more expressive character, with sharper responses and more freedom from the rear axle. Corsa prioritises precision, faster transmission behaviour and maximum performance. This range of settings contributes to the Huracán’s versatility. It can remain civilised during regular journeys before adopting a significantly more focused personality when conditions allow. Carbon-Fibre and Aluminium Chassis The Huracán was developed around a hybrid chassis combining aluminium and carbon fibre. The structure was designed to provide high torsional rigidity without excessive weight, creating a strong foundation for the suspension and drivetrain. Lamborghini’s official history identifies the original LP 610-4 as the first Huracán to introduce the LDF dual-clutch transmission and a fully digital instrument display. Further background is available in the manufacturer’s history of the Huracán’s development . cars.title: Lamborghini Sian Roadster 1 of 19
cars.description: 2021 Lamborghini Sián Roadster 1 of 19 A Brand-New, Delivery-Mileage Lamborghini Few-Off This 2021 Lamborghini Sian Roadster for sale in Dubai is one of only 19 examples produced worldwide. Presented in brand-new condition with just 100 kilometres, it is finished in an elegant White exterior over an Ivory interior. The Sián Roadster occupies an important position in Lamborghini history. It was the marque’s first open-top hybrid supercar, its first roadster to employ supercapacitor technology and one of the final few-off models developed around Lamborghini’s celebrated naturally aspirated 6.5-litre V12. While 63 examples of the Sián FKP 37 Coupé were created, production of the roofless Sián Roadster was restricted to only 19 cars. Each example was configured in close collaboration with Lamborghini Centro Stile and the Ad Personam personalisation department, ensuring that every commission carried its own identity. White Exterior with an Ivory Interior The White exterior gives this Sián Roadster a clean, sculptural appearance, allowing the complexity of its bodywork to remain clearly visible. Air channels, sharp Y-shaped elements and pronounced aerodynamic surfaces flow through the car without being visually overwhelmed by the colour. Inside, the Ivory cabin introduces a softer and more luxurious contrast. The light upholstery suits the open-air configuration particularly well, creating a bright cockpit that remains connected to the exterior design. The Sián’s cabin incorporates Lamborghini’s familiar hexagonal and Y-shaped motifs, while aluminium details and carbon-fibre surfaces reflect its position as a technological flagship. Lamborghini also developed newly designed air vents using 3D-printing technology, allowing individual components to be personalised during the original commissioning process. One of Only 19 Roadsters Worldwide The Sián belongs to Lamborghini’s exclusive “Few-Off” category, alongside models such as the Reventón, Veneno and Centenario. These vehicles are produced in extremely restricted numbers and are used to introduce new technology, materials and design concepts before they influence later Lamborghini models. Official Lamborghini production information confirms that only 63 Sián Coupés and 19 Sián Roadsters were built. This makes the Roadster substantially rarer than the Coupé and one of the lowest-production road-legal Lamborghinis of the modern era. Its name also carries a different meaning from the fighting-bull names traditionally used by the company. “Sián” translates from the local Bolognese dialect as “flash” or “lightning”, referencing the instantaneous electrical assistance provided by its innovative hybrid system. Naturally Aspirated 6.5-Litre V12 At the centre of the Sián Roadster is Lamborghini’s 6,498 cc naturally aspirated V12. Equipped with titanium intake valves and calibrated to produce 785 CV at 8,500 rpm, it was the most powerful road-going Lamborghini combustion engine at the time of the model’s introduction. Rather than replacing the character of the V12, the hybrid system was engineered to amplify it. A compact 48-volt electric motor is incorporated into the transmission, contributing an additional 34 CV. Together, the combustion engine and electric motor produce a combined 819 CV. This allows the Sián Roadster to retain the immediate throttle response, rising engine note and high-revving character of a naturally aspirated Lamborghini while using electrical assistance to improve acceleration and smooth the delivery of torque during gear changes. Lamborghini quotes a maximum speed of more than 350 km/h. Manufacturer performance figures apply to the model and have not been independently measured for this individual car. Supercapacitor Hybrid Technology Unlike a conventional hybrid vehicle, the Sián does not rely on a large lithium-ion traction battery. Instead, Lamborghini developed a lightweight supercapacitor mounted in the bulkhead between the passenger compartment and the V12 engine. According to Lamborghini’s official Sián Roadster technical information , the supercapacitor can deliver three times the power of a lithium-ion battery of the same weight while being three times lighter than a battery producing an equivalent output. The complete electrical system, including the supercapacitor and 34 CV motor, weighs just 34 kilograms. This gives the system a power-to-weight ratio of one kilogram per CV. Energy is recovered under braking and stored in the supercapacitor, which can be charged and discharged at the same rate. The stored energy is then immediately available during acceleration, rather than being retained to provide a meaningful electric-only driving range. This is a performance-led hybrid system designed to support the V12 rather than replace it. Electrical assistance remains available at speeds of up to approximately 130 km/h, helping to improve throttle response and fill the interruption in torque that would otherwise occur during transmission shifts. The electric motor can also assist during low-speed manoeuvring. Lamborghini provides a more detailed explanation of the system in its official article about the Sián’s supercapacitor hybrid technology . Seven-Speed ISR Transmission and Four-Wheel Drive The Sián Roadster uses Lamborghini’s seven-speed Independent Shifting Rod automated manual transmission. The electric motor is integrated directly into the gearbox, allowing its torque to reach the wheels without an indirect belt-driven system. Permanent four-wheel drive works with a rear mechanical self-locking differential to distribute the combined V12 and electric output. Torque distribution can be adjusted according to the selected driving mode and available grip, providing greater stability while preserving the rear-led character expected from a flagship Lamborghini. The supercapacitor system is particularly valuable during gear changes. Electrical assistance helps maintain forward momentum while the mechanical transmission completes each shift, resulting in a more continuous surge of acceleration. Four-Wheel Steering and Active Suspension Lamborghini Dynamic Steering operates alongside a dedicated rear-wheel-steering system. At lower speeds, the rear wheels can turn in the opposite direction to the fronts, effectively shortening the wheelbase and improving manoeuvrability. At higher speeds, they can turn in the same direction to increase stability. The Sián Roadster also uses magnetorheological front and rear dampers with a pushrod suspension arrangement. Damper behaviour is continuously adapted according to road conditions and the chosen driving mode, helping the chassis control roll and unwanted body movement. Specially developed Pirelli P Zero Corsa tyres work alongside the all-wheel-drive, steering and suspension systems to manage the Sián’s substantial performance. Roofless Design without Aerodynamic Compromise The Sián Roadster was designed as a completely open car rather than a Coupé with a conventional folding roof mechanism. Its uninterrupted cockpit creates a direct connection between the occupants, the surrounding environment and the naturally aspirated V12. Lamborghini engineered the body to retain aerodynamic efficiency despite the absence of a roof. Air is directed through the front splitter and bonnet, around the side intakes and outlets and towards the integrated rear spoiler. The resulting design combines a low front section, Y-shaped headlights, long aerodynamic channels and large rear buttresses. Viewed from above, its profile incorporates the “periscopio” line first associated with the original Countach. Countach-Inspired Design Details The Sián’s design looks towards Lamborghini’s electrified future while retaining deliberate references to the company’s past. The Y-shaped front lights were influenced by the Terzo Millennio concept, while the rear uses six hexagonal taillights arranged in two groups of three. Its active rear wing remains integrated into the body when not required and rises automatically during driving. This maintains the purity of the rear profile while providing additional aerodynamic support at speed. The Sián also uses patented thermally reactive cooling vanes near the exhaust system. Instead of relying on electric actuators or additional sensors, these vanes respond directly to heat. As exhaust temperatures rise, the smart-material elements change position and open the cooling channels. This elegant solution reduces mechanical complexity and demonstrates the materials-science experimentation for which Lamborghini created the Sián programme. A Landmark Collector Lamborghini The Sián Roadster represents the point at which Lamborghini began combining electrical assistance with its naturally aspirated V12. It preceded the later Countach LPI 800-4 and helped establish the technological direction that eventually led to the Revuelto. However, the Sián remains very different from Lamborghini’s later plug-in hybrid models. Its compact supercapacitor system, seven-speed automated transmission and Aventador-generation V12 give it a distinct mechanical identity. With only 19 Roadsters built, every example is important. A brand-new, delivery-mileage car showing only 100 kilometres is particularly relevant to collectors seeking a Sián in exceptionally preserved condition. The white finish highlights the model’s deeper front air channels, pronounced side sculpting and reprofiled rear section, while the twin racing stripes introduce a clear connection to Ferrari’s motorsport heritage. The Speciale’s design is not simply an aesthetic variation of the standard 458 Italia. Ferrari developed functional aerodynamic elements throughout the body, including movable front and rear devices that adjust airflow according to speed and driving conditions. The result is a design that remains elegant while serving a clear performance purpose. Red-and-Black Performance Interior Inside, this example features a purposeful Red-and-Black colour combination. Red upholstery provides a striking contrast against the darker sections of the cabin, creating an interior that feels appropriately special without distracting from the driver-focused layout. Yellow Ferrari emblems embroidered into the headrests introduce another carefully considered detail. They correspond with the Yellow exterior callipers and bring a traditional Ferrari colour into the cabin. A full interior carbon-fibre specification reinforces the car’s lightweight character. Exposed carbon creates a strong visual connection to Ferrari’s motorsport engineering while complementing the purposeful design of the dashboard, centre console and driver controls. One of Ferrari’s Definitive Naturally Aspirated V8s The 458 Speciale is powered by a 4.5-litre naturally aspirated V8. According to Ferrari’s official 458 Speciale specifications , the engine produces 605 CV at 9,000 rpm. Its exceptional power delivery and immediate throttle response are central to the Speciale experience. With no turbochargers between the accelerator and the engine, the V8 develops its performance progressively before reaching its maximum output close to the top of the rev range. Ferrari quotes acceleration from 0–100 km/h in 3.0 seconds, 0–200 km/h in 9.1 seconds and a maximum speed exceeding 325 km/h. Manufacturer performance figures are provided as model-level information and may vary according to road, tyre, weather and vehicle conditions. Seven-Speed Dual-Clutch Transmission Power is delivered to the rear wheels through Ferrari’s seven-speed dual-clutch transmission. The gearbox was calibrated specifically for the Speciale, providing faster responses and allowing the naturally aspirated V8 to remain within its most effective operating range. Controls mounted on the steering wheel give the driver direct access to indicators, lights, suspension settings and the Manettino driving-mode selector. Large fixed paddle shifters allow manual gear changes without requiring the driver to remove their hands from the wheel. Side Slip Angle Control The 458 Speciale introduced Ferrari’s Side Slip Angle Control system, commonly known as SSC. This technology analyses information such as steering angle, vehicle rotation and lateral acceleration before coordinating the traction control and electronically managed differential. Rather than removing the driver from the experience, SSC was designed to make the Speciale’s performance more accessible and controllable. It became an important part of Ferrari’s subsequent special-series and high-performance models. Ferrari’s retrospective on its special-series V8 bloodline identifies the 458 Speciale as the model that introduced SSC to this line. Lightweight Special-Series Engineering Ferrari reduced weight throughout the 458 Speciale while improving aerodynamics, engine response and chassis control. Lightweight materials, reduced cabin trim and extensive carbon-fibre components all contribute to its focused character. The suspension, steering, electronic differential and braking systems were recalibrated to work together as a complete package. The result is a car designed to provide exceptionally quick responses without losing the balance and communication for which the 458 platform became known. A Modern Ferrari Collectable The 458 Speciale occupies an important position within Ferrari’s modern history. It is one of the final and most highly developed expressions of the company’s naturally aspirated mid-engined V8 formula before Ferrari moved to turbocharged engines for its successor. This 2015 example is made particularly distinctive by its Bianco Avus exterior, twin racing stripes and carefully coordinated Yellow details. The Red-and-Black interior and full carbon-fibre specification complete a configuration that feels both highly individual and faithful to the Speciale’s motorsport-inspired purpose. cars.title: Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica
cars.description: 2023 Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica in Neon Green A Low-Mileage, High-Specification Tecnica This 2023 Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica for sale in Dubai is a visually striking specification of Lamborghini’s naturally aspirated, rear-wheel-drive supercar. Finished in Neon Green with contrasting Orange exterior accents, it features centre-lock wheels, exterior carbon-fibre trim and a coordinating Black-and-Orange interior with carbon trim and comfort seats. Showing only 4,000 kilometres, this Tecnica combines the performance-focused engineering of the Huracán STO with a more versatile and road-friendly cabin. It was created to sit between the Huracán EVO RWD and the uncompromising STO, delivering genuine circuit ability without sacrificing everyday comfort. Neon Green with Orange Accents The Neon Green exterior ensures this Huracán Tecnica has an unmistakable presence. The vivid colour highlights the model’s redesigned bodywork, from its sharper front treatment and sculpted bonnet to the prominent rear shoulders and fixed aerodynamic elements. Orange accents introduce a second layer of detail, creating a coordinated relationship between the exterior and the Black-and-Orange cabin. Their contrast against the Green paintwork emphasises individual elements of the car without concealing the lines developed specifically for the Tecnica. Unlike a standard Huracán EVO, the Tecnica received substantially revised front and rear sections. The front bumper incorporates a black Y-shaped design inspired by the Terzo Millennio concept, while reshaped air channels improve brake cooling and aerodynamic efficiency. Centre-Lock Wheels and Exterior Carbon Fibre The centre-lock wheels give this Tecnica a distinctly motorsport-influenced appearance. Their single central fastening design creates a cleaner, more technical look than a conventional five-bolt wheel arrangement and complements the model’s track-focused engineering. Exterior carbon-fibre trim adds further visual contrast and reinforces the Tecnica’s lightweight character. Rather than overwhelming the Green and Orange colour scheme, the exposed carbon provides a darker frame for the brighter exterior details. The combination of Neon Green paint, Orange accents, centre-lock wheels and visible carbon fibre gives this car a specification that feels purposefully configured rather than simply colourful. Black-and-Orange Interior The exterior colour theme continues inside with a Black-and-Orange cabin. Dark surfaces establish the performance-focused atmosphere, while the Orange sections and contrasting details create a direct visual link to the exterior accents. Interior carbon-fibre trim brings a technical finish to the cockpit, complementing the digital instrument display, aviation-inspired starter cover and driver-orientated centre console. Every primary control remains positioned within easy reach, preserving Lamborghini’s “feel like a pilot” approach. The Tecnica also received model-specific graphics for its Human-Machine Interface. The digital displays can adapt according to the selected driving mode, prioritising the information most relevant to road or circuit driving. Comfort Seats for Greater Usability This example is equipped with comfort seats rather than fixed carbon racing buckets. They provide a more accommodating seating position for regular use while retaining the support required from a 640 CV rear-wheel-drive supercar. The comfort seats suit the Tecnica’s wider purpose particularly well. The model was engineered to deliver meaningful track performance while remaining enjoyable on longer journeys and in everyday conditions. Combined with the more luxurious Black-and-Orange specification, they make this car suitable for drivers who intend to use their Lamborghini rather than reserve it exclusively for occasional circuit outings. Naturally Aspirated 5.2-Litre V10 The Huracán Tecnica is powered by Lamborghini’s naturally aspirated 5.2-litre V10, closely related to the engine used in the Huracán STO. It produces 640 CV at 8,000 rpm and 565 Nm of torque at 6,500 rpm. Unlike the all-wheel-drive Huracán EVO, the Tecnica sends its power exclusively to the rear wheels. A seven-speed Lamborghini Doppia Frizione dual-clutch transmission manages gear changes, providing rapid shifts through the steering-wheel-mounted paddles. The lack of turbocharging gives the engine an immediate response and allows its sound and power delivery to build progressively towards the upper reaches of the rev range. This naturally aspirated character is central to the Tecnica’s identity and increasingly unusual among modern supercars. According to the official Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica specifications , the car accelerates from 0–100 km/h in 3.2 seconds and from 0–200 km/h in 9.1 seconds, with a maximum speed of 325 km/h. These are manufacturer figures for the model and have not been independently tested for this individual vehicle. Rear-Wheel Steering and Direct Steering Rear-wheel steering is fundamental to the Tecnica’s handling. At lower speeds, the rear wheels can turn in the opposite direction to the front wheels, making the car feel more agile and effectively shortening its wheelbase. At higher speeds, they can turn in the same direction to increase stability. The Tecnica also uses a direct steering ratio derived from the STO. This creates a more immediate response to driver inputs and provides a closer connection between the steering wheel and front tyres. Together, these systems allow the Tecnica to feel responsive in tighter corners while remaining composed during faster direction changes. LDVI and Performance Traction Control Lamborghini Integrated Vehicle Dynamics, or LDVI, acts as the central coordinator for the Tecnica’s dynamic systems. It analyses driver inputs, vehicle movement, road conditions and the selected driving mode before adjusting the relevant settings. The Performance Traction Control System is calibrated specifically for rear-wheel drive. In Strada mode, it prioritises stability and predictability. Sport mode permits greater movement from the rear axle, while Corsa focuses on traction and precision when exiting corners. This ability to alter the car’s personality is a key part of the Tecnica’s appeal. It can feel composed and manageable during normal road use before becoming significantly more focused when Sport or Corsa mode is selected. Revised Aerodynamics and Brake Cooling The Tecnica’s body was redesigned to produce greater downforce while reducing aerodynamic drag compared with the Huracán EVO. Its extended front section, reshaped splitter, revised underbody and rear diffuser manage airflow more effectively around and beneath the car. A fixed rear wing provides additional stability without reaching the visual scale of the STO’s adjustable wing. This helps the Tecnica retain a cleaner road-car profile while still delivering meaningful aerodynamic performance. Lamborghini also developed dedicated brake-cooling channels for the front and rear discs. Air is directed towards the braking system to manage temperatures more effectively during repeated high-speed use. cars.title: Lamborghini Murcielago
cars.description: 2004 Lamborghini Murciélago LP580 in Viola Ophelia A Low-Mileage V12 Lamborghini Icon This 2004 Lamborghini Murcielago LP580 for sale in Dubai represents one of the most recognisable supercars of the early 2000s. Finished in the extraordinary Viola Ophelia exterior colour and paired with a contrasting Beige leather interior, this example has covered only 9,000 kilometres. The original Murciélago is frequently referred to by enthusiasts as the LP580, referencing its longitudinally mounted V12 engine and 580 CV output. It combines naturally aspirated performance, permanent four-wheel drive and unmistakable Lamborghini styling in a form that feels increasingly special alongside today’s electrified supercars. Striking Viola Ophelia Exterior Viola Ophelia transforms the Murciélago’s dramatic silhouette. Its rich purple finish changes character depending on the surrounding light, appearing deep and sophisticated in the shade before revealing a brighter, more expressive tone in direct sunlight. The colour works particularly well with the Murciélago’s clean wedge profile, wide rear shoulders and exceptionally low roofline. Unlike later Lamborghini designs with more intricate aerodynamic surfaces, the early Murciélago uses long, uninterrupted body lines to create its presence. Signature scissor doors provide the unmistakable visual theatre expected from a flagship Lamborghini V12. Active rear air intakes can rise from the bodywork when additional engine cooling is required, while the adjustable rear spoiler responds to speed and driving conditions. These functional elements remain neatly integrated when not in use, preserving the car’s distinctive shape. Contrasting Beige Leather Interior The Beige leather cabin provides an elegant contrast to the Viola Ophelia exterior. It gives the interior a brighter and more classical appearance while highlighting the hand-finished character associated with Lamborghini’s flagship models of this period. The cockpit is focused firmly on the driver, with a low seating position, deeply recessed instruments and controls arranged around the centre console. Its comparatively analogue layout is a major part of the Murciélago’s appeal. There are no oversized touchscreens or digitally dominated surfaces; instead, the driver is surrounded by traditional instruments, physical controls and carefully finished leather. This combination of Viola Ophelia and Beige creates a specification that feels expressive without losing the sophistication expected from a collector-grade V12 grand tourer. Naturally Aspirated 6.2-Litre V12 Mounted behind the passenger compartment is Lamborghini’s naturally aspirated 6.2-litre V12, producing 580 CV at 7,200 rpm. The engine sends its power through an automated transmission to a permanent four-wheel-drive system, giving the Murciélago strong traction while retaining the dramatic power delivery expected from a large-capacity Lamborghini V12. Lamborghini quoted acceleration from 0–100 km/h in approximately 3.8 seconds and a maximum speed of around 330 km/h. More important than the figures, however, is the character of the engine. Its response builds progressively with engine speed, accompanied by a naturally aspirated V12 soundtrack that has become increasingly rare. Lamborghini’s official history of the Murciélago confirms the original model’s 6.2-litre displacement and 580 CV output. Performance figures are manufacturer figures for the model and have not been independently measured for this individual vehicle. Permanent Four-Wheel Drive The Murciélago uses Lamborghini’s traditional layout, with its V12 positioned longitudinally behind the occupants and the transmission located ahead of the engine. A permanent four-wheel-drive system with a central viscous coupling distributes power across both axles. This mechanical configuration was engineered to provide traction and stability without diluting the car’s rear-biased supercar character. Hydraulic power steering and the absence of modern hybrid assistance preserve a more direct connection between the driver, chassis and road. Further technical information about the layout is available through Lamborghini’s official Murciélago heritage page. An Important Lamborghini Design Designed by Luc Donckerwolke, the Murciélago was the first completely new Lamborghini developed after the company joined the Audi-Volkswagen Group. Its styling incorporates references to several historic Lamborghini models, including the wedge-shaped Countach, the proportions of the Diablo and the sculptural surfaces of the Miura. The Murciélago also continued Lamborghini’s long-running naturally aspirated V12 bloodline while introducing a new standard of quality and usability for the marque. Its combination of traditional engineering, dramatic styling and limited production has made well-specified, low-mileage examples increasingly sought after. The Viola Ophelia finish makes this particular car especially memorable, although no claim is made regarding its exact production rarity without supporting factory documentation. cars.title: Mercedes Benz S550 Coupe Edition 1
cars.description: 2014 Mercedes-Benz S550 Coupé Edition 1 A Launch-Edition Luxury Coupé This 2014 Mercedes-Benz S550 Coupe Edition 1 for sale in Dubai is an elegant example of the C217-generation S-Class Coupé. Finished in Anthracite Blue with a Crystal Grey Nappa leather interior, it combines timeless grand-touring design with the exclusive equipment introduced for the Edition 1. The vehicle has covered 36,240 kilometres and is accompanied by full service history and a spare key. Its specification includes a Burmester sound system, panoramic glass roof, head-up display, 360-degree camera, ambient lighting and heated and ventilated power seats. Anthracite Blue Exterior The Anthracite Blue exterior suits the understated character of the S550 Coupé, appearing almost black under subdued lighting before revealing its deep Blue finish in brighter conditions. Its long bonnet, flowing roofline and broad rear proportions create a design that remains elegant rather than overly aggressive. Frameless side windows and the absence of a conventional B-pillar produce an uninterrupted opening when all four windows are lowered, reinforcing the open, pillarless character traditionally associated with Mercedes-Benz luxury coupés. The car is completed by 20-inch alloy wheels, which fill the pronounced wheel arches without compromising its grand-touring appearance. Edition 1 Swarovski Headlamps One of the most recognisable features of the S550 Coupé Edition 1 is its crystal detailing within the LED headlamps. Mercedes-Benz incorporated 47 Swarovski crystals into each lighting design, with 17 angular crystals forming part of the daytime running lamp and 30 round crystals used for the direction indicator. The result is a subtle but distinctive visual signature that separates the Edition 1 from a standard S550 Coupé. The crystals remain integrated within the functional lighting design, giving the front of the car a more detailed appearance without relying on additional exterior badging. Mercedes-Benz confirms the Edition 1 crystal-headlamp arrangement in its official S550 Coupé launch information . Crystal Grey Nappa Leather Interior The Crystal Grey Nappa leather interior provides a light and refined contrast against the dark Blue exterior. Its colour makes the cabin feel more spacious while allowing the sculpted dashboard, flowing door panels and individual rear seating to remain clearly defined. Nappa leather is complemented by ambient lighting, creating a calmer atmosphere during night driving. The panoramic glass roof brings additional natural light into the cabin and helps emphasise the S-Class Coupé’s wide, open interior design. Power-adjustable front seats include heating, ventilation and memory settings. These features allow the driver and passenger to save their preferred seating positions while adapting the seat temperature to changing conditions. Burmester Sound and Premium Technology The Burmester sound system provides a suitably refined audio experience for a luxury grand tourer. Its cabin-integrated speakers complement the interior design while delivering clear sound throughout the four-seat passenger compartment. A head-up display projects important information into the driver’s field of vision, reducing the need to look away from the road. The 360-degree camera and surrounding parking sensors make the large coupé easier to position in tighter spaces. The six-button centre-console control arrangement provides access to key vehicle settings, while the widescreen dashboard presentation combines driving information, navigation, media and vehicle controls within a cohesive display layout. 4.7-Litre Biturbo V8 Performance The S550 Coupé is powered by a 4.7-litre biturbo V8 producing 449 hp and 516 lb-ft of torque, equivalent to approximately 700 Nm. Power is managed through a seven-speed automatic transmission and the 4MATIC all-wheel-drive system. According to Mercedes-Benz USA’s official S550 4MATIC Coupé specifications , the model was engineered to accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 4.5 seconds. These are Mercedes-Benz’s model-level figures and have not been independently measured for this individual vehicle. The V8’s generous low-speed torque suits the character of the S-Class Coupé. Acceleration is strong and effortless, while the automatic transmission is calibrated to deliver smooth progress during more relaxed driving. 4MATIC and Air Suspension The 4MATIC system continuously distributes power between the front and rear axles, supporting traction without changing the S550’s refined grand-touring character. Air suspension provides the balance of comfort and control expected from an S-Class. It isolates the cabin from uneven surfaces while maintaining stability through faster bends and during motorway driving. The vehicle’s ride height can also be adjusted when additional clearance is required. Rather than attempting to behave like an uncompromising sports car, the S550 Coupé is engineered to cover long distances with minimal effort. Its combination of V8 performance, all-wheel-drive traction and air suspension makes it equally suitable for city use and extended journeys. Full Service History and 36,240 Kilometres This example has recorded 36,240 kilometres and benefits from full service history. The accompanying spare key adds further completeness to the vehicle’s presentation. Its Anthracite Blue and Crystal Grey specification remains elegant and distinctive, while Edition 1 features such as the Swarovski headlamps add collector interest. The Burmester audio, panoramic roof, ventilated seats, head-up display and 360-degree camera make it a comprehensively equipped luxury coupé. cars.title: McLaren 765LT Spider
cars.description: Brand-New 2022 McLaren 765LT Spider in Neon Green Limited-Production Open-Top Performance This brand-new 2022 McLaren 765LT Spider for sale in Dubai combines the most focused open-top model in McLaren’s Longtail range with a vibrant and extensively optioned specification. Its Neon Green exterior is enhanced by a full exterior carbon-fibre package, while the Black and Orange Alcantara cabin features full interior carbon. A Bowers & Wilkins sound system adds premium audio capability to a car otherwise engineered around lightweight construction, aerodynamic performance and direct driver engagement. Production of the 765LT Spider was limited to just 765 examples worldwide, making this brand-new vehicle particularly appealing to McLaren collectors. Neon Green Exterior with Full Carbon The Neon Green exterior ensures that the 765LT Spider’s elongated proportions and aerodynamically developed surfaces remain unmistakable. It creates a vivid contrast against the full exterior carbon-fibre specification, allowing the exposed weave to become an integral part of the overall design. Carbon fibre complements the 765LT’s enlarged front splitter, sculpted side sections, extended rear diffuser and active rear wing. These components were developed to increase aerodynamic load and improve high-speed stability rather than simply altering the appearance of the standard 720S Spider. The 765LT’s aggressive stance is completed by its high-mounted titanium exhaust system. Four centrally positioned outlets create one of the model’s most recognisable design features while contributing to its distinctive V8 soundtrack. Black and Orange Alcantara Interior Inside, the Black and Orange Alcantara creates a focused but highly distinctive driving environment. Black provides the foundation of the cabin, while Orange detailing introduces contrast and connects the interior with McLaren’s traditional performance colours. The full interior carbon package extends the lightweight theme throughout the cockpit. Exposed carbon-fibre surfaces reinforce the car’s structural and motorsport character, while Alcantara provides a tactile, low-glare finish suited to performance driving. The minimalist layout places the steering wheel, paddle shifters and principal chassis controls within easy reach. McLaren deliberately reduced unnecessary equipment and materials when developing the 765LT, allowing the driver to feel more closely connected to the engine, steering and suspension. Bowers & Wilkins Sound System The Bowers & Wilkins sound system adds an important layer of refinement to this particular specification. While the 765LT Spider is defined by its performance, the premium audio system makes the cabin more enjoyable during relaxed road use and longer journeys. Its inclusion is particularly notable because the Longtail philosophy traditionally places weight reduction above conventional luxury. This example therefore combines McLaren’s most focused open-top driving experience with the convenience of a high-quality entertainment system. With the roof raised, the Bowers & Wilkins system can be enjoyed in a more enclosed environment. With the roof lowered, the car’s titanium exhaust and twin-turbocharged V8 naturally become the dominant soundtrack. 765 PS Twin-Turbocharged V8 The 765LT Spider is powered by McLaren’s 4.0-litre twin-turbocharged V8, producing 765 PS and 800 Nm of torque. Power is sent exclusively to the rear wheels through a seven-speed Seamless Shift Gearbox. According to McLaren’s official 765LT Spider information , the car accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 2.8 seconds. It can reach 200 km/h in approximately 7.2 seconds before continuing to a maximum speed of 330 km/h. These are McLaren’s manufacturer figures for the 765LT Spider model and have not been independently measured for this individual vehicle. The transmission uses model-specific ratios to improve in-gear acceleration, while revised engine mapping delivers a sharper response than the 720S Spider on which the car is based. Lightweight Longtail Engineering The LT designation stands for Longtail and connects the 765LT Spider with the McLaren F1 GTR Longtail developed for endurance racing during the 1990s. Modern LT models follow the same essential principles: reduced weight, increased aerodynamic performance, greater power and more direct driver involvement. McLaren achieved a DIN weight of approximately 1,388 kilograms, making the 765LT Spider around 80 kilograms lighter than the 720S Spider. This reduction was achieved through carbon-fibre body components, lighter glazing, a titanium exhaust and extensive changes throughout the cabin and chassis. Despite being a convertible, the Spider requires no heavy additional structural reinforcement. Its carbon-fibre Monocage II-S structure provides the rigidity necessary for precise suspension control, helping the open-top model preserve the responses of the 765LT Coupé. Retractable Hardtop The single-piece electric retractable hardtop can be opened or closed in approximately 11 seconds. Its compact operation allows the 765LT Spider to change from an enclosed supercar into a fully open performance car with minimal interruption. A powered rear window can also be lowered independently when the roof remains in place. This allows more of the titanium exhaust note into the cabin without opening the complete roof. With the top lowered, the Black and Orange interior becomes a prominent part of the exterior presentation. Neon Green paintwork, exposed carbon fibre and the contrasting cabin combine to create a specification that is dramatic from every angle. Track-Focused Aerodynamics and Chassis The 765LT Spider uses an extended front splitter, wider front track and revised suspension geometry to increase precision and stability. The active rear wing alters its position according to braking, acceleration and aerodynamic requirements. McLaren’s interconnected hydraulic suspension system manages body control without relying on conventional anti-roll bars. The driver can adjust the powertrain and handling settings independently, allowing the car to be configured for road use or more demanding circuit driving. Carbon-ceramic brakes provide the stopping performance required for a vehicle capable of reaching 200 km/h in little more than seven seconds. The combination of lightweight construction, rear-wheel drive and hydraulic steering gives the 765LT Spider a particularly communicative character. Brand-New Collector Opportunity This 2022 example is offered in brand-new condition, adding to its appeal as one of only 765 765LT Spiders produced. Its Neon Green exterior ensures immediate visual impact, while the full exterior and interior carbon packages create a specification closely aligned with McLaren’s Longtail philosophy. The Black and Orange Alcantara interior introduces further individuality, and the Bowers & Wilkins sound system adds everyday enjoyment without diluting the car’s performance-led identity. cars.title: Lamborghini Huracan STO
cars.description: 2023 Lamborghini Huracán STO in Matt Black A Stealth-Finished Road-Legal Racing Machine This 2023 Lamborghini Huracan STO for sale in Dubai combines the model’s track-focused engineering with a particularly menacing specification. Its Matt Black exterior is complemented by exposed carbon-fibre elements, while the Alcantara interior introduces distinctive Green accents and further carbon trim. STO stands for Super Trofeo Omologata , a name that communicates the model’s close connection to Lamborghini Squadra Corse. Inspired by the Huracán Super Trofeo EVO and GT3 EVO racing cars, the STO was engineered to transfer motorsport-derived aerodynamics, lightweight construction and chassis technology into a road-homologated supercar. Matt Black Exterior with Carbon Fibre The Matt Black exterior gives this Huracán STO a stealthy appearance while allowing its complex aerodynamics to remain clearly visible. The non-reflective finish emphasises the bonnet vents, roof scoop, rear shark fin and large adjustable wing without distracting from the car’s underlying design. Exterior carbon-fibre components complement the Matt Black bodywork while supporting the STO’s lightweight philosophy. The contrast between the paint and the exposed weave becomes more apparent at close range, giving the exterior additional depth without compromising its restrained colour scheme. Unlike styling components added purely for appearance, the STO’s aerodynamic elements have a functional purpose. Every intake, vent and surface was developed to manage cooling, reduce lift or generate stability at higher speeds. The Carbon-Fibre Cofango One of the Huracán STO’s defining features is its Cofango. The name combines the Italian words cofano , meaning bonnet, and parafango , meaning wing or fender. This large carbon-fibre structure incorporates the bonnet, front wings and bumper into one component. It can be opened forwards to reveal the front section of the car, creating an unmistakable connection with competition machinery. According to Lamborghini’s official Huracán STO information , carbon fibre is used for more than 75 per cent of the model’s exterior body panels. The STO is also 43 kilograms lighter than the Huracán Performante, reflecting the level of attention given to every component. Alcantara Interior with Green Accents The interior continues the performance-led theme with extensive Alcantara upholstery. Its soft, low-glare finish is well suited to a focused driving environment, while the Green accents introduce a vibrant contrast against the predominantly dark cabin. Interior carbon fibre reinforces the connection between the road car and Lamborghini’s racing programme. The material adds a technical finish to the cockpit while remaining consistent with the weight-saving approach used throughout the STO. Rather than concealing the car’s mechanical character, the cabin is designed to make it part of the experience. Reduced insulation allows more of the naturally aspirated V10 and transmission to be heard, while the driving position places the steering wheel, paddles and digital instruments directly within the driver’s line of sight. 640 CV Naturally Aspirated V10 Behind the cabin is Lamborghini’s 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10, producing 640 CV at 8,000 rpm and 565 Nm of torque at 6,500 rpm. Power is delivered exclusively to the rear wheels through a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission. Lamborghini quotes acceleration from 0 to 100 km/h in 3.0 seconds and from 0 to 200 km/h in 9.0 seconds. Maximum speed is rated at 310 km/h. These are Lamborghini’s manufacturer specifications for the Huracán STO model and have not been independently measured for this individual vehicle. The absence of turbocharging or hybrid assistance gives the STO a progressive, high-revving power delivery. Throttle response is immediate, and the engine note becomes increasingly intense as the V10 approaches the upper reaches of its rev range. Aerodynamics Developed for the Track At the front, the splitter and bonnet ducts manage airflow beneath and through the body. Louvred front wings help release pressure from the wheel housings, while the rear diffuser and roof-mounted air intake contribute to stability and engine cooling. The tall rear shark fin helps control airflow during cornering. Behind it, the manually adjustable rear wing provides three settings, allowing the aerodynamic balance to be altered according to the driver’s intended use. These features give the STO an appearance that is dramatic but never arbitrary. Its design follows the requirements of performance, cooling and aerodynamic efficiency. Motorsport-Derived Braking and Driving Modes The STO uses Brembo CCM-R carbon-ceramic brake technology derived from motorsport applications. A dedicated cooling system directs air towards the brakes to help manage temperatures and maintain consistency during demanding driving. Three model-specific driving settings alter the car’s behaviour. STO mode is calibrated for engaging road use, Trofeo prepares the vehicle for dry circuit conditions, and Pioggia adjusts the electronic systems for wet or low-grip surfaces. Direct steering, rear-wheel drive and dedicated traction-control calibration give the STO a more immediate character than the standard Huracán. Its systems are designed to support the driver while preserving the physical feedback expected from a track-focused Lamborghini. A Distinctive Collector Specification The combination of Matt Black paintwork, exterior carbon fibre and an Alcantara cabin with Green accents gives this 2023 STO a particularly cohesive identity. Carbon-fibre interior elements complete the specification, connecting the visual presentation with the model’s lightweight engineering. As one of the most focused derivatives of Lamborghini’s naturally aspirated V10 platform, the STO already holds an important position within the Huracán range. This dark, carbon-rich specification further enhances its appeal to enthusiasts seeking a road-legal Lamborghini with an authentic connection to Squadra Corse. cars.title: Lamborghini Revuelto
cars.description: 2024 Blue Lamborghini Revuelto with Full Carbon For Sale in Dubai A Bespoke V12 Hybrid Supercar This 2024 Lamborghini Revuelto for sale in Dubai combines Lamborghini’s revolutionary V12 hybrid performance with an exceptionally desirable carbon-fibre specification. Its striking Blue exterior is enhanced by the full exterior carbon package, while the Black and White interior features full carbon trim and distinctive Q-Citura stitching. With only 1,000 kilometres recorded, this Revuelto presents an opportunity to acquire a lightly driven example of Lamborghini’s first High Performance Electrified Vehicle. Its dramatic colour combination complements the model’s advanced engineering while retaining the unmistakable character of a flagship Lamborghini V12. Blue Exterior with Full Carbon Package The Blue exterior highlights the Revuelto’s complex surfaces, sharp body lines and aeronautically inspired proportions. Contrasting exposed carbon fibre adds definition to its aerodynamic profile, creating a more technical and performance-focused appearance. The full exterior carbon specification complements the Revuelto’s active aerodynamic systems and carbon-intensive construction. Its Y-shaped LED lighting, pronounced side intakes, exposed engine bay and high-mounted hexagonal exhaust outlets produce a design that is immediately identifiable as a modern Lamborghini. Active aerodynamics continuously manage airflow around the vehicle. The electronically controlled rear wing can change position according to the selected driving mode and vehicle conditions, balancing lower drag with increased aerodynamic stability. Black and White Q-Citura Interior Inside, the Black and White upholstery creates a highly distinctive contrast. Black surfaces establish a focused cockpit, while the White sections brighten the cabin and draw attention to Lamborghini’s detailed craftsmanship. Q-Citura stitching introduces the geometric upholstery pattern closely associated with Lamborghini’s Ad Personam interiors. Rather than relying solely on contrasting colours, the stitching adds texture and visual depth across the cabin. The full interior carbon package continues the exterior theme, surrounding the occupants with lightweight, performance-led materials. Carbon-fibre components reinforce the connection between the passenger compartment and the advanced structure beneath it. Three digital displays divide information between the driver, central infotainment system and passenger. The passenger display allows selected performance and journey information to be viewed without distracting the driver from the road. 1,015 CV Hybrid V12 Powertrain The Revuelto is powered by a newly developed 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12 combined with three electric motors. Two electric motors are positioned at the front axle, while a third is integrated with the transmission, producing a combined output of 1,015 CV. Power is managed through a new eight-speed dual-clutch transmission, the first application of this gearbox technology in a production Lamborghini V12. Its compact transverse positioning behind the engine helps improve weight distribution while creating space for the hybrid battery within the centre tunnel. According to Lamborghini’s official Revuelto specifications , the car accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 2.5 seconds and can reach a maximum speed exceeding 350 km/h. These are Lamborghini’s manufacturer figures for the Revuelto model and have not been independently measured for this individual car. Lamborghini’s First V12 HPEV The Revuelto is officially described as Lamborghini’s first V12 High Performance Electrified Vehicle. Unlike a conventional hybrid designed principally around efficiency, its electrical system supports acceleration, torque distribution and dynamic response. The two front electric motors provide independent torque to each wheel, supporting all-wheel drive and active torque vectoring. The third motor can assist the rear axle or operate as a generator depending on the selected mode and battery requirements. Lamborghini provides 13 different driving configurations by combining its Città, Strada, Sport and Corsa settings with Recharge, Hybrid and Performance energy strategies. This allows the Revuelto to move between electric urban driving and the full output of its V12 hybrid system. The official Revuelto launch information confirms that the V12, three electric motors and dual-clutch transmission were developed as one integrated performance architecture. Advanced Carbon-Fibre Construction Carbon fibre is fundamental to the Revuelto rather than simply a decorative option. The vehicle uses what Lamborghini calls a monofuselage, combining a carbon-fibre monocoque with a front structure manufactured from Forged Composites. This construction increases structural rigidity while reducing weight compared with a traditional aluminium front frame. It also provides a suitably advanced foundation for the car’s hybrid powertrain, active aerodynamics and sophisticated suspension systems. The full exterior and interior carbon specification of this particular example builds upon that structural engineering. The visible carbon components allow the materials beneath the Revuelto’s performance to become an integral part of its appearance. A Low-Mileage Collector Specification With only 1,000 kilometres recorded, this Blue 2024 Revuelto remains a lightly driven example. Its full exterior carbon, full interior carbon and Black and White Q-Citura cabin create a specification that stands apart from more conventionally configured cars. The naturally aspirated V12 preserves Lamborghini’s most important mechanical tradition, while the hybrid system introduces a new level of performance and control. This makes the Revuelto a significant model in the company’s history: both the successor to the Aventador and the beginning of Lamborghini’s electrified V12 era. cars.title: Lamborghini Murcielago Roadster | Ad Personam
cars.description: 2008 Lamborghini Murciélago LP640 Roadster in Nero Nemesis An Ad Personam V12 Lamborghini with Only 6,000 Kilometres This 2008 Lamborghini Murcielago LP640 Roadster for sale in Dubai is an exceptional example of Lamborghini’s naturally aspirated V12 flagship. Commissioned through the Ad Personam programme, it is finished in the dramatic Nero Nemesis exterior colour and paired with a contrasting Red leather interior featuring Lamborghini’s distinctive Q-Citura stitching. Showing only 6,000 kilometres, this remarkably low-mileage Roadster combines an individual factory specification with the theatrical design and mechanical character that made the Murciélago one of the defining supercars of its generation. Signature Hercules wheels complete the exterior, giving the car an unmistakable stance while remaining faithful to its original Lamborghini identity. Ad Personam Nero Nemesis Exterior Nero Nemesis is a particularly appropriate finish for the Murciélago LP640 Roadster. Its matt-effect Black appearance emphasises the car’s sharp body lines, wide rear haunches and low, cab-forward proportions without distracting from the underlying design. The Ad Personam specification adds further collector appeal, reflecting Lamborghini’s factory personalisation programme and allowing the car to stand apart from conventionally configured examples. Classic Murciélago details include vertically opening scissor doors, large side air intakes and active rear cooling intakes that rise when additional airflow is required. The open rear deck and Roadster-specific engine cover give this version a character distinct from the LP640 Coupé. Hercules Wheels and Iconic Road Presence The Hercules wheels provide a strong finishing detail, complementing the dark exterior while preserving the period-correct appearance of the LP640 Roadster. Their bold design suits the Murciélago’s substantial proportions and leaves its dramatic bodywork as the main visual focus. With the roof removed, the car’s extremely low windscreen, exposed cabin and broad rear bodywork create a silhouette unlike any contemporary supercar. A manually fitted soft top provides temporary weather protection, but the Murciélago Roadster is at its most dramatic when experienced as a fully open V12 Lamborghini. Red Leather with Q-Citura Stitching The Red leather interior creates a vivid contrast against the Nero Nemesis exterior. Lamborghini’s Q-Citura stitching introduces a recognisable geometric pattern across the upholstery, giving the cabin a more detailed and individual character than a conventional leather specification. Although the Murciélago’s interior provides the essential comfort expected from a flagship supercar, its layout remains strongly focused on the driver. The low seating position, prominent centre tunnel and steeply angled windscreen create an enclosed cockpit, even when the roof is removed. The E-Gear transmission is operated through steering-column-mounted paddles, allowing the driver to control the six-speed automated manual gearbox without taking their hands away from the steering wheel. Its deliberate, mechanical shift character is an important part of the Murciélago driving experience. Naturally Aspirated 6.5-Litre V12 Mounted behind the occupants is Lamborghini’s 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12. The LP640-4 version produces 640 CV at 8,000 rpm, with power delivered through a permanent four-wheel-drive system. Lamborghini’s own history of the Murciélago V12 confirms that the LP640 represented a significant evolution from the original 6.2-litre Murciélago, increasing output from 580 CV to 640 CV. The larger engine, revised electronics and updated transmission gave the LP640 stronger performance while retaining the naturally aspirated response that defines Lamborghini’s traditional V12 models. With no turbocharging or hybrid assistance, the engine’s character develops progressively as the revs rise. In Roadster form, the sound and physical sensation of the V12 become even more prominent, particularly with the roof removed. A Roadster with Its Own Character The LP640 Roadster was more than a Murciélago Coupé with its roof removed. Lamborghini made dedicated changes to the structure, bodywork and passenger compartment to give the open model its own identity. According to the official Lamborghini Murciélago LP640 Roadster archive , the cabin was specifically arranged around the driver, while the asymmetrical exterior theme was echoed inside the vehicle. This unusual approach gives the Roadster a distinctive visual character from either side. The experience is equally individual. The scissor doors, manual roof arrangement, E-Gear transmission and open-air V12 soundtrack transform every journey into an event in a way that few modern supercars can replicate. Very Low Mileage and Collector Appeal With only 6,000 kilometres recorded, this 2008 example offers the very low mileage sought after by collectors of important naturally aspirated Lamborghinis. Its appeal is strengthened by the Ad Personam Nero Nemesis finish, contrasting Red Q-Citura leather and desirable Hercules wheels. The Murciélago also occupies an important position in Lamborghini history. It succeeded the Diablo and became the company’s first new V12 flagship of the 21st century, while retaining the traditional mid-mounted, naturally aspirated twelve-cylinder layout. This combination of rarity, specification and remarkably limited use makes the car suitable for a dedicated collection while preserving the opportunity to experience one of Lamborghini’s most theatrical open-top models. cars.title: Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica
cars.description: Brand-New 2024 Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica in Green Naturally Aspirated V10 Performance with a Striking Specification This brand-new 2024 Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica for sale in Dubai combines the model’s naturally aspirated performance with a vibrant, carefully coordinated specification. Its Green exterior is paired with a Black and Green interior featuring carbon-fibre trim and supportive bucket seats. Positioned between the road-focused Huracán EVO and the uncompromising STO, the Tecnica was developed to provide a more versatile interpretation of Lamborghini’s rear-wheel-drive V10 platform. It delivers the performance and precision required for demanding roads while retaining the comfort and usability expected from a modern Lamborghini. Offered as a brand-new example, this 2024 Huracán Tecnica provides an opportunity to experience one of the final and most accomplished developments of Lamborghini’s naturally aspirated V10 supercar. Green Exterior with Purposeful Aerodynamics The Green exterior gives the Tecnica an unmistakable road presence, emphasising its sharp lines, low proportions and aerodynamically driven design. Black exterior elements provide contrast, allowing the Green paintwork to stand out while maintaining the car’s technical, performance-focused appearance. Lamborghini redesigned the front and rear architecture of the Tecnica to increase stability, improve downforce and reduce aerodynamic drag. The front bumper incorporates pronounced air channels and a distinctive Y-shaped design, while the fixed rear spoiler, revised diffuser and vertical rear window clearly separate the Tecnica from other Huracán variants. Its styling takes inspiration from Lamborghini’s motorsport programme and the Huracán Super Trofeo EVO2, but the overall design remains suitable for both road and track environments. Black and Green Interior The Black and Green cabin continues the exterior’s bold colour theme. Black materials establish a focused foundation, while Green detailing gives the interior a bespoke and immediately recognisable character. Carbon-fibre interior trim reinforces the Tecnica’s lightweight engineering and adds a technical finish throughout the driver-focused cockpit. The bucket seats provide increased lateral support, making them particularly appropriate for a car designed to deliver precise handling and high cornering performance. Rather than overwhelming the driver with unnecessary decoration, the cabin places the principal controls, digital instruments and driving-mode selector within immediate reach. Dedicated Tecnica graphics further distinguish the interface from other members of the Huracán family. 640 CV Naturally Aspirated V10 The Huracán Tecnica is powered by a 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 producing 640 CV at 8,000 rpm and 565 Nm of torque at 6,500 rpm. Its engine is closely related to the unit used in the Huracán STO, combining immediate throttle response with a progressive delivery that becomes increasingly intense as the revs rise. Power is transmitted exclusively to the rear wheels through Lamborghini’s seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox. This configuration creates a distinctly engaging character, allowing the driver to experience the balance and adjustability associated with a rear-wheel-drive supercar. According to Lamborghini’s official Huracán Tecnica specifications , the model accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 3.2 seconds and reaches 200 km/h in 9.1 seconds. Its maximum speed is rated at 325 km/h. These are Lamborghini’s manufacturer figures for the Tecnica model and have not been independently measured for this individual vehicle. Advanced Chassis Technology The Tecnica uses Lamborghini Integrated Vehicle Dynamics, commonly known as LDVI, to coordinate the car’s steering, traction control, suspension and powertrain responses. The system processes driver inputs and road conditions to adapt the vehicle’s behaviour to the selected driving mode. Rear-wheel steering improves agility at lower speeds while supporting stability during faster motorway driving. A more direct steering ratio provides immediate responses, helping the driver place the vehicle accurately through corners. Lamborghini’s Performance Traction Control System is calibrated differently across the Strada, Sport and Corsa settings. Strada prioritises confidence and stability, Sport allows greater movement and driver involvement, and Corsa prepares the car for more focused performance driving. The transmission can operate smoothly during everyday driving or provide quicker, more assertive shifts when Sport Plus or Track mode is selected. At higher speeds, it contributes to straight-line stability and more controlled cornering behaviour. Dynamic Torque Vectoring works alongside the differential, applying subtle braking adjustments to individual wheels when required. Double-wishbone front suspension and a multi-link rear arrangement are supported by adaptive dampers with Skyhook technology. Sport Plus sharpens the car’s responses and increases the presence of the active exhaust, while Track mode delivers the firmest and most immediate configuration. Speed-sensitive steering remains light enough for city use but gains weight as speed increases, providing clearer feedback during faster driving. Everyday Usability Although engineered as a dedicated sports car, the Vantage remains manageable during daily journeys. Front and rear parking sensors assist in confined spaces, while the central infotainment display provides access to navigation, Bluetooth connectivity and vehicle settings. The rear luggage compartment provides useful space for weekend bags or shopping, while the front-mid-engine layout avoids many of the practicality compromises associated with mid-engined supercars. This balance makes the Vantage particularly appealing to buyers seeking an engaging sports car that can still be used regularly. Privacy Suite and Additional Phantom EWB Options The wider Phantom Extended options catalogue includes the remarkable Privacy Suite. Rear-wheel steering improves manoeuvrability at lower speeds and stability on faster roads, ensuring that the Phantom Extended remains composed despite its substantial dimensions. Retractable Hardtop Design The 488 Spider uses a folding metal hardtop that allows it to function as both a closed coupé and an open-air supercar. When raised, the roof follows the clean lines of the cabin and provides greater insulation than a conventional fabric hood. Lowering the roof gives the driver a more direct experience of the V8 engine and exhaust note. The compact roof mechanism was engineered around the car’s mid-rear-engined layout, preserving the balanced proportions and aerodynamic form of the 488. This dual character makes the Spider especially appealing in Dubai, where it can be enjoyed with the roof lowered during cooler weather while retaining the comfort and security of a hardtop during the warmer months. Black and Blue Interior Inside, the two-tone black and blue cabin creates a direct visual connection with the exterior. Black provides a focused foundation, while blue sections and details add colour without distracting from the driver-oriented layout. The cabin places the steering wheel, transmission paddles and principal driving controls within immediate reach. Ferrari’s steering-wheel-mounted Manettino allows the driver to adjust the car’s dynamic settings without removing their hands from the wheel. The colour combination is complemented by the extensive carbon-fibre interior package. Its woven finish introduces a strong contrast against the softer cabin materials and reinforces the link between this road car and Ferrari’s competition experience. Full Interior Carbon-Fibre Package Carbon fibre extends throughout the driver zone and central areas of the cabin, making this example feel substantially more special than a 488 Spider equipped with only isolated carbon options. The material complements the instrument surround, steering-wheel area, paddle shifters and centre bridge, creating a cohesive performance-focused environment. The extensive carbon specification is especially effective when the roof is lowered, as the interior details become clearly visible alongside the blue exterior. Together, the full interior and exterior carbon packages give this car a unified specification rather than the appearance of individual options added separately. 670 CV Twin-Turbocharged V8 The 488 Spider is powered by a 3.9-litre twin-turbocharged V8 producing 670 cv at 8,000 rpm and 760 Nm of torque. Power is transmitted to the rear wheels through Ferrari’s rapid seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox. According to Ferrari’s official 488 Spider specifications , the car accelerates from 0–100 km/h in 3.0 seconds and reaches 200 km/h in 8.7 seconds. Its maximum speed exceeds 325 km/h. Variable Torque Management delivers power progressively through the transmission’s ratios, while Side Slip Control 2 coordinates the electronic differential, traction control and adaptive dampers. This technology allows the 488 to deliver remarkable performance while remaining approachable during everyday road driving. Available from Exotic Cars Dubai The blue paintwork, coordinated black and blue cabin, full exterior carbon and full interior carbon combine to create a particularly distinctive 488 Spider. The illuminated Spirit of Ecstasy , the gloss black Pantheon grille , and the sweeping LED headlight signature announce this vehicle's identity with the quiet, absolute confidence that only Rolls-Royce can project. White on the Spectre is a statement of both purity and vision — the perfect colour for a car that marks the beginning of a new chapter in automotive history. Interior — Tri-Colour Cabin, Starlight Headliner & Bespoke Luxury Inside the Spectre, Rolls-Royce's Bespoke team has created a cabin of extraordinary individuality and artistry. The tri-colour interior — three carefully chosen leathers woven together across the seats, dashboard, and door panels — creates a visual depth and chromatic richness that transforms every surface into a work of considered craft. cars.title: Bentley GT W12
cars.description: 2004 Bentley Continental GT W12 – Black An Early Modern-Era Bentley This 2004 Bentley Continental GT W12 for sale in Dubai combines timeless British grand-touring design with the effortless performance of Bentley’s original twin-turbocharged W12 powertrain. Finished in a classic black exterior over a tan leather interior, this first-generation Continental GT has covered 110,000 kilometres and is offered with warranty availability. As a 2004 example, it belongs to the earliest production period of the model that transformed Bentley into the modern luxury and performance manufacturer recognised today. Timeless Black Exterior The black exterior highlights the Continental GT’s flowing roofline, muscular rear haunches and substantial proportions. Its design combines the elegance of a traditional Bentley coupé with a considerably more modern and athletic stance. At the front, the large matrix grille and four individual headlamps create an unmistakable identity. Along the sides, the gently rising waistline leads towards the pronounced rear wheel arches, giving the Continental GT a sense of movement even when stationary. More than two decades after its introduction, the first-generation Continental GT remains immediately recognisable. Its restrained black finish helps preserve the sophisticated character of the original design. Tan Leather Interior Inside, the tan leather interior creates a warm and traditional contrast against the black exterior. The cabin was designed to accommodate four occupants while retaining the intimate atmosphere expected from a luxury grand tourer. Bentley craftsmanship is evident throughout the interior, from the stitched leather surfaces to the substantial metal controls and hand-finished trim. The symmetrical dashboard wraps around the occupants, creating a cabin that feels both formal and driver-focused. Unlike a conventional two-seat sports car, the Continental GT provides usable rear seating and luggage space. This allows it to remain suitable for daily driving, longer journeys and weekends away without sacrificing its coupé proportions. The Bentley That Began a New Era Introduced in 2003, the first-generation Continental GT was the first completely new Bentley of the company’s modern era. It was also the marque’s first production model to use all-wheel drive and the innovative W12 engine. Bentley describes the original Continental GT as the model that began the company’s modern renaissance, combining traditional Crewe craftsmanship with contemporary performance and technology. This 2004 example therefore represents more than an early luxury coupé. It belongs to the first chapter of a model line that has remained central to Bentley for over two decades. Correct 6.0-Litre W12 Performance Although the advert’s engine field currently shows a 4.0-litre V8, this GT W12 is powered by the correct 6.0-litre twin-turbocharged W12 engine. According to Bentley’s official Continental GT history and specifications , the original engine develops 560 PS, equivalent to approximately 552 bhp, and 650 Nm of torque. Power is delivered through a six-speed ZF automatic transmission and permanent all-wheel drive. The W12’s broad torque delivery allows the Bentley to accelerate smoothly from low engine speeds, making rapid progress without requiring constant gear changes. Bentley quoted acceleration from 0 to 100 km/h in approximately 4.8 seconds and a maximum speed of 318 km/h. These figures remain impressive for a full four-seat luxury coupé introduced more than twenty years ago. All-Wheel Drive and Air Suspension The Continental GT’s permanent all-wheel-drive system uses a Torsen centre differential to distribute power between the axles. This provides reassuring traction during acceleration and helps the vehicle remain stable across changing road conditions. Air suspension and electronically controlled damping allow the car to combine long-distance comfort with controlled handling. The system continually responds to vehicle speed and road conditions, maintaining the composed character expected from a Bentley. Although the GT possesses considerable performance, it was designed primarily as a grand tourer. Its strengths are effortless motorway pace, a refined cabin and the ability to cover significant distances without tiring its occupants. An Appealing Modern Classic Early Continental GT models are increasingly appreciated for their design, historical importance and distinctive W12 powertrain. Bentley ended production of its twelve-cylinder engine in 2024, giving the original W12-powered models additional significance within the marque’s history. The black-over-tan colour combination suits the car’s character particularly well. It is traditional enough to feel timeless while allowing the Continental GT’s proportions and interior craftsmanship to remain the focus. With 110,000 kilometres recorded, this example is offered with warranty availability for additional reassurance. Full warranty terms and coverage can be confirmed with the Exotic Cars sales team.
